---
title: "A3 self-check — Gas exchange and flow"
---

Explain each answer before opening the callout. See the [tutorial](index.qmd)
for the complete transport path.

## 1. Is ventilation the same as diffusion into the blood?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. Ventilation moves the environmental medium by bulk flow. Diffusion crosses
an exchange barrier down a local driving gradient. Perfusion supplies blood
to the other side of that barrier.
:::

## 2. If area doubles and thickness doubles, with all else unchanged, what happens to predicted transfer?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

It is unchanged in the simple proportional model: $2A/(2L)=A/L$. Real organs
also have heterogeneous flow and gradients, so the comparison is conditional.
:::

## 3. Is countercurrent exchange an example of oxygen diffusing uphill?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. Opposite flow directions can maintain a gradient along the exchange
path. At each location oxygen still moves down the local partial-pressure
gradient. Comparing remote inlet and outlet values confuses position with
local exchange.
:::

## 4. Does a normal oxygen partial pressure guarantee normal blood oxygen content?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. Oxygen content also depends strongly on haemoglobin amount and binding.
The same partial pressure can coexist with different total oxygen amounts
per litre of blood. Pressure, saturation and content are distinct quantities.
:::

## 5. Are pulmonary arteries named incorrectly because their blood is relatively deoxygenated?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and veins return it. The names
refer to direction relative to the heart, not oxygenation state.
:::

## 6. Flow is 3 L min⁻¹ and arterial–venous content difference 40 mL O₂ L⁻¹. What oxygen-use rate follows?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

$3\times40=120$ mL O₂ min⁻¹ under the stated steady-state assumptions.
Litres of blood cancel. Substituting a partial-pressure difference would
not give the required amount balance.
:::
